texts.li: [tale,winter] {X_nameDef}, a storyteller of {FACTION}, came in out of the snow asking for a seat near the hearth, and offers a winter's worth of stories in exchange. One of them is about this colony: "{TALE}"

[notale,summer] With a sunburned nose and a hat full of feathers, {X_nameDef}, a storyteller of {FACTION}, would like to spend the evening. There'll be stories in the yard after supper, while it's still light enough to see faces.

[notale,skill:Social] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} tells stories for a living, and has already found {A_nameDef}, who tells them for nothing. They've agreed to take turns tonight, and to argue about the endings.

[tale,lowtech] A bard of {FACTION} named {X_nameDef} has come to the gate with a harp on {X_possessive} back. {X_nameDef} has made a song about the colony out of what people say on the road, and wants to try it on the people it's about: "{TALE}"

[tale,!lowtech] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} collects stories from the settlements and tells them at the next one. The colony is in {X_possessive} collection now, told like this: "{TALE}" {X_nameDef} would like supper and a bed, and to hear the colony's side.

[notale,colony:Open] {X_nameDef}, a storyteller of {FACTION}, heard on the road that this colony welcomes travelers, and has come to see. {X_nameDef} will pay for supper and a bed in stories, as many as anyone wants to hear.
[winter] Travelers from {FACTION} are coming through the snow to stand at {DEAD}'s grave. They knew {DEAD} long before the colony did, and say they won't stay past the evening.
[spring] People of {FACTION} are on their way with the first spring flowers for {DEAD}'s grave. They knew {DEAD} before the colony did, and would like a little while at the grave before they go.

[colony:Traditional] Kin of {DEAD} from {FACTION} are coming to honor the grave, and sent ahead to ask whether the colony keeps the old rites for its dead. It keeps the ones it can. They'll stay the afternoon.
[!lowtech] A message came from {FACTION}: family of {DEAD} are on the road and would like to see the grave. They'll be quiet, and gone by evening.

[lowtech] An old friend of {DEAD} is walking in from {FACTION}'s lands with a few others, carrying a jug of the drink {DEAD} liked. They want to pour some on the grave, the way it's done where {DEAD} came from.
[summer] Pilgrims of {FACTION} have stopped at the colony, burned by the sun and out of water as well as food. They ask for a meal and a drink, and the shade of the wall for an afternoon.
[colony:Generous] Pilgrims of {FACTION} say they heard on the road that the colony never turns the hungry away. They're thin and footsore, and they've come to see if it's true.
[colony:Thrifty] A band of pilgrims of {FACTION} have stopped outside. They've heard this colony doesn't give much away, and ask anyway, very politely, for one meal before they go on.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} found a band of pilgrims of {FACTION} resting by the road, too hungry to go on, and has brought their request to the council: one meal each, and they'll be on their way.
[lowtech] Pilgrims of {FACTION} have come up the road ringing small bells, on their way to a shrine three valleys away. Their bags are empty, and they ask for a meal.
[!lowtech] A group of pilgrims of {FACTION} have walked in off the old highway with a hand-drawn map to a holy place and nothing left to eat. They ask whether the colony can spare a meal.

lines.li: [winter] The pilgrims ate around the hearth, steaming as they thawed out, and thanked their hosts twice over before going back into the cold.
[lowtech] The pilgrims ate everything they were given and rang their little bells for the colony as they left. They'll speak well of it on the road.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} served the pilgrims with {A_possessive} own hands and made sure the smallest of them had seconds. They'll speak well of the colony all down the road.
[winter] The pilgrims bowed and went back out into the cold, hungry.
The pilgrims thanked the colony for nothing, very politely, and walked on.

texts.li: [medieval] A mule loaded with books stands at the gate. Its owner, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a master from one of the great libraries, asks for a bed for the night. {A_nameDef} mentioned the colony's work on {TALE}, and {X_nameDef} has been leafing through {X_possessive} books for something on it ever since.

[spacer] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, a research lead between postings, asks for a bunk for the night. On hearing about the colony's work on {TALE}, {X_nameDef} asks to see the notes, and then for a pencil.

[winter] {X_nameDef}, a traveling scholar of {FACTION}, has been caught out by the snow and asks to wait out the night. {X_nameDef} noticed the colony's notes on {TALE} on the table and has offered to pay for the bed with a few ideas.

[skill:Intellectual] {A_nameDef} has been stuck on {TALE} for days. Tonight a traveling scholar, {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, asked for a bed, and {A_nameDef} has already pulled up a second chair at the desk.

[industrial] {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} repairs machines from town to town and reads everything {X_pronoun} can carry. {X_nameDef} asks for a place to sleep, and on hearing about the colony's work on {TALE}, offers to take a look over breakfast.

lines.li: [skill:Intellectual] {A_nameDef} and {X_nameDef} filled the table with notes, and were still arguing about {TALE} long after the rest of the colony had gone to bed.
[lowtech] {X_nameDef} talked {A_nameDef} through the old writings by candlelight, and the work on {TALE} came a long way that night.
{X_nameDef} nodded, wished the colony luck with {TALE}, and walked on to the next settlement.

texts.li: [!lowtech] {X_nameDef}, barely grown, has come up the road with a pack and a list of questions about {SKILL}, all of them for {A_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} heard about {A_nameDef} from a trader and asks to stay and learn.

[Cooking] {X_nameDef}, a young cook from somewhere with worse food, has come a long way to learn from {A_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} brought {X_possessive} own knife, and is ready to start with the peeling.
[Medicine] {X_nameDef} wants to be a healer, and has heard that {A_nameDef} is the best for miles around. {X_nameDef} asks to stay and learn, and promises to boil every bandage.

[Construction] {X_nameDef} has watched {A_nameDef}'s walls go up from the road for a week, and today walked up to the gate and asked to learn how. {X_nameDef} wants to stay as {A_nameDef}'s apprentice.

[Plants] {X_nameDef}, a farm hand who wants more than hand work, has heard that nothing dies in {A_nameDef}'s fields. {X_nameDef} asks to stay and learn from {A_nameDef}, and has brought {X_possessive} own hoe.

[Crafting] {X_nameDef} has a sack of things {X_pronoun} made and wants {A_nameDef} to say what's wrong with every one of them. {X_nameDef} asks to stay as {A_nameDef}'s apprentice and learn {SKILL} properly.

lines.li: {X_nameDef} moved in with one bag, and was at the first lesson before {A_nameDef} was.
{X_nameDef} went back down the road. {A_nameDef} watched from the gate, and was short with everyone at supper.

texts.li: [winter] A stranger has been sheltering against the colony wall since the snow started, and asks to come in and stay. {X_nameDef} gives a name and nothing else. {A_nameDef} found {X_objective} first, half frozen, and thinks {X_nameDef} is running from something.
[outlaw] {A_nameDef} knows the look of someone running from the law, having worn it once. {X_nameDef} has it. {X_nameDef} turned up at the gate this morning, asks to stay, and won't say where from.

[soldier] {X_nameDef} walked in and asked to stay, standing straight the whole time like someone trained to it for years. {A_nameDef}, who soldiered once, noticed. {X_nameDef} won't talk about the past.

[colony:Open] Word on the road is that this colony takes people in. {X_nameDef} heard it and has come to ask to stay. {X_nameDef} is polite and strong, and says almost nothing about where {X_pronoun} has been.

lines.li: [winter] {X_nameDef} came in out of the cold and stayed. Whatever {X_nameDef} was running from hasn't followed {X_objective} here.
{X_nameDef} gave the council a long look, shouldered {X_possessive} pack, and went back the way {X_pronoun} came.

texts.li: [lowtech] {A_nameDef} found a child crying in the long grass out past the fields. It's {X_nameDef}, of {FACTION}, who followed a goat too far and lost the way home. Somewhere a family is calling for {X_objective}.

[!lowtech] A child walked out of the treeline this morning holding a broken toy and asking for {X_possessive} mother. It's {X_nameDef}, of {FACTION}, a long way from home. {A_nameDef} has given {X_objective} something to eat, and {X_possessive} family will be out looking.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} carried a lost child in from the fields: {X_nameDef}, of {FACTION}, who has stopped crying now that there's bread. The family can't be far behind, and must be frantic.
[winter] A stray {THING}, all ribs and frozen fur, has followed {A_nameDef} home through the snow and is lying against the door. It isn't going anywhere.
[skill:Animals] {A_nameDef} has been feeding a stray {THING} by the fields for days. Today it followed {A_objective} home and sat down by the door as if it lived here.
[trait:Kind] {A_nameDef} came home with a stray {THING} in {A_possessive} arms, thin and limping, and has already made it a bed near the hearth.
[summer] A stray {THING} has been lying in the shade by the well since noon, and every time {A_nameDef} walks past, it gets up and follows. It looks like it means to stay.

lines.li: [child] The {THING} sleeps in {A_nameDef}'s bed now. The council was never asked about that part.
The {THING} ate two bowls of scraps and fell asleep in a patch of sun. It lives here now.
{A_nameDef} carried the {THING} out to the road and left it with a bit of food. It was still sitting there when {A_nameDef} looked back.
